Compute within-host diversity indices

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/diversity.R
calcDiversity.Rd

Generic for computing diversity metrics from within-host variant data. Methods should return a DataFrame with one row per sample.

Calculates diversity metrics per sample from a WithinHostExperiment. Implements standard population genetics indices adapted for deep sequencing iSNV data, following Lauring (2020).

Usage

calcDiversity(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment'
calcDiversity(
  x,
  indices = c("shannon", "pi", "watterson", "richness", "simpson", "chao1"),
  usePassedOnly = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A WithinHostExperiment.

...

Not used; supplying anything is an error.

indices

Character vector. Which indices to compute: "shannon", "pi", "watterson", "richness", "simpson", "chao1" (default: all six).

usePassedOnly

Logical. If TRUE (default), only use variants where qcPass == TRUE.

Value

A DataFrame of diversity metrics.

A DataFrame with one row per sample and columns sample_id, n_sites_assessed, detection_limit and one column per requested index.

Details

Genome length. "pi" and "watterson" are per site and divide by the genome length, which is read from seqlengths(rowRanges(x)) as the summed length of every sequence recorded there, including segments of a segmented genome on which no site lies. It is a property of the reference the calls were made against, not a number to type: readWithinHost records it from the VCF header's ##contig lines or from a DNAStringSet passed as genome, and annotateCodonChange from its reference. When it is not recorded the function stops and says how to record it, for example seqlengths(x) <- c(seg = 29903L).

For "watterson", the sample's median read depth is passed as the sample size \(n\), which for the reasons given in tajimaD makes \(\theta_W\) small; calcNeutralityTests caps \(n\) instead, so the two need not agree.

Reading a zero. A diversity of zero means something different when the sample had no call at all, when every call failed QC, and when calls were present but below the frequency QC allows. Two columns keep these apart: n_sites_assessed, the number of sites at which the sample has a frequency, before QC, and detection_limit, the lowest frequency a call could have kept through the filters applied (the strictest minFreq among them), NA when no filter was applied or usePassedOnly = FALSE. richness counts the sites that entered the indices after QC: the segregating sites, whose frequency lies strictly between 0 and 1. A frequency of 0, or of 1, a fixed difference from the reference such as iVar reports, is not segregating within the host, so it enters none of the indices; the site count of "watterson" and the singletons and doubletons of "chao1" come from the same sites. A site counts as assessed only when the sample has a call there: a VCF lists only the sites a caller reported, so a site sequenced without a call cannot be told apart from one not sequenced at all, and neither is counted.

References

Lauring AS (2020). Within-Host Viral Diversity: A Window into Viral Evolution. Annu Rev Virol 7:63-81. doi:10.1146/annurev-virology-010320-061642

Examples

vcf <- system.file("extdata", "test_donor.vcf",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
## the genome length comes from the reference, recorded on import
ref <- Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(system.file("extdata",
    "test_ref.fa", package = "WithinHostExperiment"))
whe <- readWithinHost(vcf,
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(sample_id = "donor"),
    caller = "ivar", genome = ref)
calcDiversity(whe)
#> DataFrame with 1 row and 9 columns
#>     sample_id n_sites_assessed detection_limit  richness   shannon         pi
#>   <character>        <integer>       <numeric> <integer> <numeric>  <numeric>
#> 1       donor               15              NA        15   7.00462 0.00454524
#>    watterson   simpson     chao1
#>    <numeric> <numeric> <numeric>
#> 1 0.00188569    4.5424        15
